title: Assemble
rule: Heroes, villains and supporting characters from Marvel's comics, films and shows; code names and real names both count.

traps.Hellboy: Published by Dark Horse, not Marvel.

fact: Fin Fang Foom, a dragon-like alien, debuted in 1961 in Strange Tales #89 and was later made one of Iron Man's enemies.

title: Ka-pow!
rule: Heroes, villains and supporting characters published by DC, in comics, films and shows; code names and real names both count.

traps.Hellboy: Published by Dark Horse, not DC.

fact: Harley Quinn debuted in Batman: The Animated Series in 1992 and did not join mainline DC comics continuity until 1999.

title: Wand waving
rule: Any named spell, charm, jinx, hex or curse from the books, films or official games; potions and magical objects don't count.

traps.Portkey: A magical object, not a spell.
traps.Sorting Hat: A magical object, not a spell.

fact: J.K. Rowling said Avada Kedavra comes from the Aramaic word that became abracadabra, which originally meant 'let the thing be destroyed'.

title: Muppet mayhem
q: A Muppet or Sesame Street character
rule: Puppet characters from the Muppet shows and films or from Sesame Street; human cast members don't qualify.

traps.Barney: A purple dinosaur from a different children's show.
traps.Sooty: A British glove puppet, not a Muppet.
traps.Zippy: A puppet from the British show Rainbow, not a Muppet.
traps.Lamb Chop: Shari Lewis's puppet, not a Muppet.
traps.Mr. Hooper: A human shopkeeper on Sesame Street, not a puppet.

fact: Oscar the Grouch was orange in Sesame Street's first season and turned green in the second.

title: Pop idols
q: A boy band or girl group
rule: Pop vocal groups of three or more marketed as boy bands or girl groups, K-pop included; mixed-gender groups don't count.

traps.S Club 7: A mixed-gender group of boys and girls.
traps.Steps: A mixed-gender group of boys and girls.
traps.Hear'Say: A mixed-gender group of boys and girls.
traps.Beatles: A rock band, not a boy band.
traps.Wham!: A duo, not a group of three or more.

fact: Puerto Rican group Menudo kept replacing members as they grew up, so most left around 16; Ricky Martin joined at 12.

title: Drive-thru
q: A fast food or restaurant chain
rule: Chains serving meals or snacks in the UK or US, current or defunct; coffee-only and ice-cream-only chains don't count.

traps.Tesco: A supermarket, not a restaurant chain.

fact: Little Chef's British founder, Sam Alper, got the idea after spotting a Little Chef diner in Leedey, Oklahoma, in 1958.
